svg.title: Redis & Valkey
svg.desc: Redis & Valkey. An in-memory data-structure server: cache, session store, rate limiter, leaderboard and lightweight queue in one process. Step 1, Where it sits: Three stateless app servers share one Redis: a cache, sessions, a rate limiter and a leaderboard. Step 2, One command at a time: Commands wait in line and run one at a time: INCR returns 101, over 100, so app-1 answers 429. Step 3, Durability and failover: Writes go to the AOF and, later, to the replicas. The primary dies: an unreplicated write is lost. Step 4, Scale out, and the limits: Cluster: 16,384 hash slots over primaries; multi-key commands need one slot. Memory is the hard cap.

g.text: Three stateless app servers share one Redis: a cache, sessions, a rate limiter and a leaderboard.
Commands wait in line and run one at a time: INCR returns 101, over 100, so app-1 answers 429.
Writes go to the AOF and, later, to the replicas. The primary dies: an unreplicated write is lost.
Cluster: 16,384 hash slots over primaries; multi-key commands need one slot. Memory is the hard cap.
session store shared by all 3 apps
each call is one network round trip,
answered from memory with no disk read
the app servers keep no state, so any
of them can serve any user
one command at a time, in arrival order:
a key is deleted once its TTL runs out
every write is appended to the AOF
and queued for the replicas, which
lose about the last second of writes
the whole dataset lives in RAM
noeviction (the default): new writes fail with OOM
allkeys-lru: evict the least recently used keys
over to a replica if it dies
each shard is a primary with
